newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Uneximbank sees Sibneft protest soon.
newsitem.headline: Russia Uneximbank sees Sibneft protest soon.

text.p: Russia's third biggest bank by assets Uneximbank said on Thursday it hoped to launch a legal challenge to the results of last week's tender for 51 percent of oil group Sibneft in the next few days.

Uneximbank press secretary Modest Kolerov told Reuters the bank, whose bid for the majority stake in the oil group was rejected at a tender earlier this week, was waiting for official written confirmation of the results before starting proceedings.
"As soon as we get the protocol we will put together a statement and will definitely go to court," Kolerov said.
"In the view of our lawyer there were clear violations in the tender conditions and in the way it was carried out."
He claimed the tender organisers were deliberately being obstructive by insisting on mailing the documents necessary to file a protest.
"I hope we'll get the documents in the next few days," Kolerov said, adding that Uneximbank has 30 days from the date the tender results were announced to file a protest in court.
An unknown company called OOO Finansovaya Neftyanaya Korporatsiya (FNK) won the tender with a bid of $110 million against a starting price of $101 million.

The 51 percent stake had been held in trust by another little-known oil industry investment vehicle, ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK), which is controlled by business magnate and presidential security adviser Boris Berezovsky.
Berezovsky, whose company took control of the Sibneft stake in 1995 under the government's shares for loans scheme with a credit to the state of $100.3 million, has denied links to FNK.
Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft) is Russia's seventh largest oil group and is chaired by Gazprom chairman Rem Vyakhirev. Its main production unit is Noyabrksneftegaz.
In 1996 ZAO Rifile-Oil won 15 percent of shares and ZAO Sins won 19 percent. The ownership of these two companies has not been published.
Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) owns 85 percent of SIDANKO, Russia's fifth biggest oil group, and a 38 percent stake in Norilsk Nickel.
